stops.name: Gerhard Berger
stops.note: 'at the end of the fifth was into the pits': tyres plus a split intercooler-to-engine crossover tract changed; 'Two laps down'. Lane time far above a tyre stop. His second tyre stop: no lap

stops.name: Nelson Piquet
stops.note: 'On lap 15, though, Piquet headed into pit lane' (Autosport; Wikipedia's chart has Rosberg leading from lap 15). Motor Sport says 'he stopped on lap 16': Autosport kept. Wheels changed in 'around eight seconds' (Motor Sport, stationary)

stops.name: Nelson Piquet
stops.note: 'at the end of lap 27 the McLaren was in front once more, for the Williams was coming in again' (Autosport; Wikipedia's chart: Rosberg leads laps 27-38). Motor Sport says 'He stopped again on lap 28': Autosport kept

stops.name: Nigel Mansell
stops.note: 'He came in at the end of lap 17' (Piquet took the tyres readied for him on lap 15)

stops.name: Keke Rosberg
stops.note: 'Rosberg duly came in after 19 laps' (Wikipedia's chart: Prost leads lap 20)

notes: Autosport 'Grand Prix Gold: German GP 1986' (its contemporary report) and Motor Sport Sep 1986 (DSJ). Missing: Berger's second tyre stop, Tambay's (#16) early stop for lost wheel weights, Brundle's (#3) stop for a new black box (no laps), every other midfield stop. Storyline is fuel: the 195-litre limit; Rosberg and Prost ran minimum boost all race and both ran dry on the last lap (Rosberg second at the start of it, at the first chicane; Prost, fourth after Senna passed him late on, in the stadium's last two corners). Both classified a lap down (43 laps, Jolpica 'Out of fuel'). Senna also ran out just past the line. Wikipedia's text says 45 laps; its infobox, Motor Sport, Autosport and Jolpica say 44.
